novel_features.name: Series search
novel_features.description: Find the right BLS series ID by plain-English title, survey, or area without leaving the terminal.
novel_features.rationale: BLS publishes no public series-search endpoint; every existing wrapper leaves discovery to the user. Only a locally-synced FTS5 index over the BLS flat-file series catalog makes this possible.
novel_features.example: bls-pp-cli series search "Los Angeles CPI all items" --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when you need the canonical BLS series ID for a concept (any indicator, any area, any survey) before fetching values. Without it, agents either hallucinate IDs or rely on a hand-curated dictionary.
novel_features.group: Discovery the live API can't do

novel_features.name: Macro snapshot
novel_features.description: One command returns the current state of the U.S. macro economy: headline + core CPI, U3, payrolls, JOLTS openings, PPI, ECI, productivity, with YoY and MoM changes.
novel_features.rationale: Combines a curated ~15-series cross-survey batch with BLS's server-side calculations:true flag. Replaces a dashboard that today requires opening FRED in a browser and pasting series IDs into a notebook.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you want a single read of the U.S. labor and price-stability picture without composing a 15-series request yourself.

novel_features.name: Release calendar
novel_features.description: List upcoming BLS releases (CPI, employment situation, JOLTS, PPI...) with date, time, and news-release URL.
novel_features.rationale: BLS publishes the release calendar only as HTML behind Akamai bot protection. A locally-curated table refreshed by sync turns that into a queryable surface (and survives shutdown reshuffles).
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to plan around BLS data drops; combine with --watch to poll until the next print lands.

novel_features.name: Footnote decoder
novel_features.description: Decode BLS footnote codes (P, R, C, ...) into plain-English explanations.
novel_features.rationale: The live API returns footnote codes but never their text; only the flat-file footnote tables hold the explanations. A local join solves it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an observation comes back with footnotes you don't recognize — preliminary vs revised vs corrected matters for the analyst writeup.
novel_features.group: Discovery the live API can't do

novel_features.name: Historical extremum
novel_features.description: Compute max, min, and percentile rank of a series's latest observation across a configurable window from the local cache.
novel_features.rationale: BLS returns a window of values, never extrema. SQL over the local observations cache answers "is this the highest since X" in one call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for release-day writeups, agent tool-calls that need historical context, and quickly answering "have we been here before" without scrolling FRED charts.

novel_features.name: SA vs NSA compare
novel_features.description: Show seasonally-adjusted and not-seasonally-adjusted variants of a series side-by-side.
novel_features.rationale: BLS encodes seasonal adjustment in position 3 of the packed series ID. The local seasonal-adjustment lookup table makes a one-command pairing possible.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you need to disambiguate whether a trend you're seeing is genuine or a seasonal artifact.

narrative.headline: The first feature-rich CLI for the BLS Public Data API — with offline series search, a release calendar, footnote decoding, and a one-command macro snapshot that no Python or R wrapper offers.
narrative.value_prop: BLS publishes hundreds of thousands of labor and economic time series behind packed structural IDs like CUUR0000SA0 and LNS14000000, and the live API has no way to search for them. bls-pp-cli ships a locally-synced series catalog with FTS5 search, a curated U.S. macro snapshot, the release calendar, and footnote decoding — the things every analyst, reporter, and agent needs but no existing wrapper provides. Every command is also an MCP tool, so LLM agents can resolve series IDs and fetch values without a hand-curated dictionary.
narrative.auth_narrative: BLS API works without a key (25 queries/day, 3 series per request, 10 years of history). A free registration key from https://data.bls.gov/registrationEngine/ unlocks 500 queries/day, 50 series per request, 20 years, and the calculations / catalog / annual-average flags. Set with `bls-pp-cli auth set-token <key>` or `BLS_API_KEY=<key>` in your environment.

quickstart.comment: One-time: stash your free BLS registration key in the local config so every command can use it.
Bulk-imports the BLS flat-file series catalog, surveys, areas, items, and footnotes into a local SQLite store. Takes a few minutes; run monthly.

quickstart.command: bls-pp-cli series search "Los Angeles CPI all items" --json
quickstart.comment: Find the canonical BLS series ID by plain English instead of bouncing through bls.gov/cpi/tables.
Fetch the L.A. CPI-U with server-side YoY/MoM changes.
Pull the current U.S. macro dashboard (CPI, core CPI, U3, payrolls, JOLTS openings, PPI, ECI, productivity) in one call.
See which BLS releases are coming up so you know when to refresh.

troubleshoots.fix: Free unauthenticated tier is 25 queries/day. Register at https://data.bls.gov/registrationEngine/ and run `bls-pp-cli auth set-token <key>` for 500/day.

troubleshoots.symptom: Series ID not found by `series search`
troubleshoots.fix: The local catalog may be stale or missing the survey. Run `bls-pp-cli sync` to refresh from BLS flat files.
BLS returns empty for IDs that don't exist (no 404). Verify the ID with `bls-pp-cli series search <plain-english>` or `bls-pp-cli sql 'SELECT id FROM series WHERE id = ?'`.

troubleshoots.symptom: Server-side calculations are missing from the response
troubleshoots.fix: `calculations:true` requires a registered key. Set BLS_API_KEY and pass --calc.
download.bls.gov is bot-walled. The CLI ships a browser-realistic user-agent and a polite rate limit; if you still get 403, run with `--source api-only` to skip flat-file enrichment.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for bls-pp-cli when you need authoritative U.S. labor or price-stability data and you don't want to bounce between FRED, bls.gov data tools, and Python notebooks. The CLI is best for: (1) workflows where series-ID discovery is the bottleneck; (2) cross-survey snapshots that touch multiple BLS surveys at once; (3) agent contexts where every command is also an MCP tool. Skip it if you need exotic vintage/revision history beyond what BLS publishes through the API — only the live values are mirrored.
